tool.name: Gadgetron – MCP
tool.description: Connect MCP servers and offer OmniWrench as an MCP server to other AI programs.
tool.long_description: Connects external MCP servers (HTTP or local programs, protocol version 2026-07-28 and older): their tools become functions for the chat panel and all AI tools, with the AI access level of Gadgetron and confirmation for anything that changes something. OmniWrench can also act as a local MCP server for other AI programs (Claude Desktop, VS Code …), protected by a token; changes are confirmed here in the program. For clients that only speak stdio: OmniWrench --mcp-stdio.
mcp.title: MCP
mcp.intro: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) connects AI programs with tools. At the top, external MCP servers can be connected so that the assistants can use their tools. At the bottom, OmniWrench itself can be switched on as an MCP server for other AI programs (e.g. Claude Desktop, VS Code).
mcp.col.name: Name
mcp.client_hint: The tools are available to the assistants in the chat panel and all AI tools while Gadgetron is open. The AI access level of Gadgetron applies: read-only tools from level 3 (read), all others from level 4 and only after confirmation.
mcp.server_hint: The server is only reachable on this computer (127.0.0.1) and requires the token. It runs while Gadgetron is open. It offers the functions the built-in assistants have, with the same access levels and the same pseudonymization. A separate level for external programs can be set under "AI access" → exceptions → "MCP server". Changes are always confirmed here in the program.
mcp.name: Name:
mcp.stdio_warning: The command runs on this computer with the rights of the signed-in user. Only add servers from a trusted source.
mcp.trusted_tip: Without trust every tool counts as changing: it needs level 4 and a confirmation before each call.
mcp.tools_hint: Unchecked tools are not offered to the assistants.
